newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON MAKES LOW-KEY START TO ATHENS CAMPAIGN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON MAKES LOW-KEY START TO ATHENS CAMPAIGN.

text.p: Michael Johnson made a low-key start to the world championships on Sunday in front of a small crowd which would have disappointed the promoter of a national meeting.
The Olympic 200 and 400 metres champion, allowed to compete as a defending champion despite missing the U.S. trials, easily won his first round 400 metres heat in 45.66 seconds.
Only about 3,000 people were present to watch Johnson goes through his paces on a hot, sunny morning, many of them from the international media.
But Johnson was unconcerned about the sparse crowd and lack of atmosphere in his first major race since he lost in Paris in June, his first defeat over 400 in eight years.
"I came in confident. My objective is just to get through every round as comfortably and easily as possible," he said.
"Up until this point the season has been very frustrating but I am glad to be healthy now."

Johnson, who injured his left quadriceps in the 150 metres show down with Donovan Bailey in Toronto on June 1, was allowed to compete after the world governing body changed its rules just before the championships and awarded wild cards to defending champions for the first time.

He took control of the race with a strong burst down the back straight, coming off the final bend ahead but used the muscles in his neck more that those in his legs over the final 100 metres as he slowed up and looked around for late bursts from his rivals.
The American was effectively jogging when he crossed the line in the eighth fastest time. Compatriot Jerome Young clocked the swiftest time of 45.34.
